$D_n(G)=G\cap(1+\Delta^n)=\{g\in G: g-1\in\Delta^n\}$, where $\Delta$ is the augmentation ideal of $\mathbb Z[G]$. Always $\gamma_n(G)\subseteq D_n(G)$; for $n\le3$ this is an equality, for $n=4$ in general it is not (Rips). The quotient $D_n(G)/\gamma_n(G)$ is abelian (Gupta–Kuz'min), and its exponent is bounded by a function of $n$ alone (Sjögren).

The ideal $\Delta=\Delta(G)$ of the ring $\mathbb Z[G]$, the kernel of the augmentation $\sum a_g g\mapsto\sum a_g$; as an abelian group it is generated by the elements $g-1$, $g\in G$. Its powers define the dimension subgroups: $D_n(G)=\{g\in G: g-1\in\Delta^n\}$.

$\gamma_1(G)=G$, $\gamma_{n+1}(G)=[\gamma_n(G),G]$, the subgroup generated by the commutators $[a,b]=a^{-1}b^{-1}ab$ with $a\in\gamma_n(G)$, $b\in G$. The nilpotency class of $G$ is the least $c$ with $\gamma_{c+1}(G)=1$.
$[a,b]=a^{-1}b^{-1}ab$, so $ab=ba[a,b]$. This is the convention of the D5 paper (explicitly in Theorem 6.17 and Appendix C).

For a finite $p$-group $Q$: $M_n(Q)=Q\cap(1+\Delta_{\mathbb F_p}(Q)^n)$, the dimension subgroups modulo $p$; by Jennings (and Lazard) $M_n=\prod_{ip^j\ge n}\gamma_i^{p^j}$. Since $\mathbb Z[Q]\to\mathbb F_p[Q]$ maps $\Delta^n$ into $\Delta_{\mathbb F_p}^n$, always $D_n(Q)\subseteq M_n(Q)$.
For a $p$-group $Q$: $P_1(Q)=Q$, $P_{i+1}(Q)=[P_i(Q),Q]\,P_i(Q)^p$. The $p$-class of $Q$ is the least $c$ with $P_{c+1}(Q)=1$. Always $\gamma_i\subseteq P_i$, and $P_2=\Phi(Q)$.

For a finite $p$-group $P=F/R$, $F$ free of rank $d(P)$: $P^*=F/[R,F]R^p$ (O'Brien). Its subgroup $M=R/[R,F]R^p\le Z(P^*)$ is the multiplier (elementary abelian, $P^*/M\cong P$), and $N=P_{c+1}(P^*)\le M$ is the nucleus ($c$ the $p$-class of $P$). The immediate descendants of step 1 of $P$ are the $P^*/U$, where $U<M$ has index $p$ and $N\not\le U$.
The subgroup $M=R/[R,F]R^p$ of the $p$-covering group $P^*=F/[R,F]R^p$ of $P=F/R$: central, elementary abelian, with $P^*/M\cong P$.

$N=P_{c+1}(P^*)\le M$, where $P^*$ is the $p$-covering group of the $p$-group $P$, $M$ its multiplier and $c$ the $p$-class of $P$. $P$ has immediate descendants (is nonterminal) if and only if $N\ne1$.

If the $p$-class of a $p$-group $Q$ is $c\ge2$, then $Q$ is an immediate descendant of $Q/P_c(Q)$ of step $\log_p|P_c(Q)|$. The descendants of step 1 of $P$ are the $P^*/U$, where $P^*$ is the $p$-covering group and $U$ a subgroup of index $p$ of the multiplier not containing the nucleus. The $p$-group generation algorithm (ANUPQ) lists them up to isomorphism.

A $2$-group $Q$ of nilpotency class $3$ with cyclic centre whose involution $n$ lies in $\gamma_3(Q)\cap M_5(Q)$, and of $2$-class $c\ge4$ with $P_c(Q)=\langle n\rangle$. By Lemma 5.2 a finite $2$-group of class $3$ with $D_5(Q)\ne1$ and $D_5(Q/N)=1$ for every central $N$ of order $2$ is a candidate. In the proof of Theorem 6.19 the candidates are the step-1 descendants of order $3^9$ and class $4$ with $Q''\ne1$, cyclic centre and $z\in Q''\cap M_5$.
For a $p$-group $Q$ of nilpotency class $c$, the tuple $(a_1,\dots,a_c)$ with $p^{a_i}=|\gamma_i(Q)/\gamma_{i+1}(Q)|$; for example $(3,2,2,1)$ or $(3,3,1,1)$ for $p=3$.

Kourovka Notebook, Problem 20.84 (Question 1.1 of the D5 paper): is $D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for every group $G$? Equivalently, $D_5(Q)=1$ for every finite $2$-group $Q$ of nilpotency class $3$ (Proposition 2.1). A related open question is whether $3$-torsion occurs in $D_5/\gamma_5$ (§7, item 2).
Status: paper: proved; computer: computer-assisted; open: an open question; Lean: formally verified; more on what is formally verified in Lean is on the Blueprint page.
Question 1.1 Kourovka Notebook, Problem 20.84 open
Is it true that $D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for every group $G$?
Proposition 2.1 Reduction to 2-groups of class 3 paper
The following conditions are equivalent:
$D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for every group $G$;
$D_5(M)=1$ for every metabelian group $M$ of nilpotency class at most $3$;
$D_5(Q)=1$ for every finite metabelian $2$-group $Q$ of nilpotency class exactly $3$.
(Every group of class $\le3$ is metabelian, so the word "metabelian" can be dropped — Remark 2.2.)
Lemma 5.2 Minimal counterexample paper
Let $Q$ be a finite $2$-group of nilpotency class $3$ with $D_5(Q/N)=1$ for every central subgroup $N$ of order $2$. If $D_5(Q)\ne1$, then
(a) the centre $Z(Q)$ is cyclic and $D_5(Q)=\Omega_1(Z(Q))=\langle n\rangle$ has order $2$;
(b) $n\in\gamma_3(Q)\cap M_5(Q)$;
(c) the $2$-class $c$ of $Q$ is at least $4$ and $P_c(Q)=\langle n\rangle$;
(d) $Q$ is an immediate descendant of step $1$ of $R=Q/\langle n\rangle$, which has nilpotency class $2$ or $3$, $2$-class $c-1\ge3$ and cyclic $\gamma_3(R)$.
Proposition 5.3 Order 2¹⁰ computer
$D_5(Q)=1$ for every $2$-group $Q$ of order $2^{10}$ and nilpotency class $3$ (all of them are metabelian). By computer.
